forecaster_note: Surf Guru read: the swell landed. 7.0ft @ 9s from 184° — dead south — averaging ~862 kJ through the morning and peaking near 1,222 kJ. That 184° angle is exactly the direction Dee Why hates: the headland eats it, so DY only pulls chest-to-overhead (2–3ft) while Long Reef, fully exposed, runs overhead to well overhead at 3–5ft on the identical swell. Curl Curl splits it at 2–4ft; North Steyne is shadowed down to thigh-to-stomach. Wind is the clock today — W/WSW offshore at 12–14 kph until roughly 10:30am, then SSW cross by 11 and dead S by 1pm. Surfline's read matches: 'Much more obvious looking day to target… winds blow WSW in the AM for clean surf at most, then trend more S/SW for cleaner surf towards the southern ends.' So it's dawn to 10:30 or don't bother. Friday repeats it almost exactly (7.4ft @ 10s from 177°, ~951 kJ) with the same morning-only shape. The real prize is Sunday: 6.6ft @ 12s from 146° at ~1,166 kJ under a NW/NNW offshore (306–324°) all morning. Twelve seconds from 146° is finally off the shadow line, and the Point gets fed properly for the first time this run. Saturday is the throwaway — energy drops to ~547 kJ with 2.3ft @ 6s E chop mixed in. Water 18.5°C. ✈️ Worth saying out loud: you're in Oahu from today through 13 Aug, so this entire run happens without you — run /hawaii-surf over there instead. 🦈 SharkSmart live feeds (SMART drumline, DPI drone, SLSNSW, trauma, events) read clear — no Northern Beaches detections in the last 24h; most recent nearby were Long Reef and Dee Why drone sightings on Sat 25 Jul. — Surfline Sydney forecast + SharkSmart NSW

wind.summary: W offshore at dawn (262°, 12 kph gusting 21) backing WSW through to about 10:30am at 14 kph — light and clean. Then it swings SSW (204°) by 11am and dead S (169°) by 1pm, which flattens the shape everywhere except the southern corners. Morning-only window.

shark.summary: No Northern Beaches detections (Palm Beach → Manly) in the last 24h. DPI drone, SLSNSW, SMART drumline, trauma and events feeds all read clear this morning. Most recent nearby: Long Reef and Dee Why drone sightings on Sat 25 Jul — 5 days ago.

days.label: Today
days.note: Best morning of the week and it's a morning only. ~862 kJ from a 7.0ft @ 9s dead-S swell (184°), W/WSW offshore until roughly 10:30am then SSW cross by 11 and dead S by 1pm. Dead-S means Long Reef is the pick at 3–5ft while Dee Why sits shadowed at 2–3ft. The 8:49am high fills the banks right through the good window — 6:50 to 10:30am is the session.

swells.label: Dead-S mid-period groundswell — the one angle Dee Why is shadowed from
Tiny NE windswell trace — no push in it

dee-why.window: 6:50–10:30am. The Point is the only corner that bends a 184° dead-S into a rideable wall — sit wide and let it wrap. The open beachie banks will be closing out with 862 kJ behind them. After 11am the SSW cross takes the shape out of it.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: Frontside at the Point, which is the only place this swell is worth surfing here. Nine-second period at 862 kJ is a lot of push with not much face — take off deeper than feels comfortable and get one committed bottom turn in before it fattens on the inside. The wider sets wrap best on the 8:49am high.

long-reef.window: Pick of the coast. Full exposure to the 184° S — solid overhead-plus sets on the full 862 kJ. Dawn to 10:30am while the W/WSW holds.
alerts: Well overhead with 862 kJ behind it — pick your paddle channel off the headland before you jump in, not after.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: The Reef corner runs right, so this is your frontside. At 3–5ft on a dead-S the difference between a set wave and a closeout is entirely where you sit — a little further north than the crowd, off the reef edge, so you can use the channel to get back out.

curl-curl.window: The sensible middle — real size and punch without Long Reef's consequence. Best 7:00–10:00am; the W/WSW sits a touch straighter offshore here than at Dee Why.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Curl Curl's lefts are your backhand and they need exactly this much swell to bank up — 2–4ft on a dead-S is when they work. Keep your weight forward through the first turn; on a 9-second period the wave outruns you if you stall to set up.

manly.window: Shadowed hard — thigh-to-stomach on a swell that's well overhead at Long Reef. It rates fair-to-good at 7am purely because it's clean, not because there's a wave in it. Only worth the drive if the northern banks look too heavy.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Steyne is the most sheltered of the four and today is the day that shows. If you end up here it's a small-wave backhand session on the lefts — you'll be generating all the speed yourself, the swell won't do it for you.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: A near-repeat of today and marginally stronger: 7.4ft @ 10s from 177°, ~951 kJ, still dead south. Same shape to the day — WSW offshore 10–13 kph to about 10:30am, SSW cross by 11, S onshore by 1pm. Long Reef holds the size at 3–5ft, Dee Why stays shadowed at 2–3ft, Curl Curl steps up to head-high-plus on the extra second of period.

dee-why.window: 7:00–10:30am. The extra second of period (10s vs today's 9s) makes the Point wrap slightly better than Thursday — still the only workable corner on a 177° swell.

long-reef.window: Biggest again and heavier than Thursday on the longer period. Dawn to 10:30am under the WSW.
alerts: 3–5ft at 951 kJ and 10 seconds — the strongest morning of the week at this bank. Size up.

curl-curl.window: Steps up a notch on the 10s — head-high plus with real punch. Best 7:00–10:00am.

manly.window: A touch more than Thursday but still the shadowed option. Waist-to-shoulder and clean until the wind swings around 11am.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Sunday is the session of the whole run; Saturday is filler. Saturday: energy drops to ~547 kJ on a fading 6.0ft @ 10s from 168° with 2.3ft @ 6s E chop mixed in — clean under a W/WSW offshore all day, just soft. Sunday: 6.6ft @ 12s from 146° at ~1,166 kJ with a NW/NNW offshore (306–324°) holding through the morning. Twelve seconds from 146° is finally off Dee Why's shadow line — the first time this run the Point gets properly fed.

dee-why.window: Sunday 7:00–10:30am is the pick of the weekend and of the week — 12s from 146° wraps into the Point instead of being shadowed, under a clean NW offshore. Saturday is smaller and softer at ~547 kJ and only worth a cruise.

long-reef.window: Biggest of the four across both days. Sunday runs to double overhead on 1,166 kJ with a N/NNW offshore — early only, the wind goes NNE by 11am.
alerts: Sunday 4–5ft at 1,166 kJ and 12 seconds — the heaviest water of the run. Step up and go at first light.

curl-curl.window: Punchy both days, best Sunday dawn to mid-morning under the NW. Handles the 12s with a lot less consequence than Long Reef.

manly.window: The manageable option — clean chest-high-plus Sunday morning, a size down on the northern banks as always. Saturday dawn is the one time all weekend it rates fair-to-good here.
